messages:
sam: Quick flag — starter sample started failing on Node 18 after I pulled latest canary. Dynamic import resolves to commonjs entry and crashes with "Cannot use import statement outside a module".

jordan: can you show package.json exports?

sam: here's the snippet:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
  },
  "./utils/*": "./dist/utils/*.js"
}
```

lee: did the pack step actually include the esm file in the tarball? sometimes our builder omits it when built with --only-cjs.

sam: checked the tarball — only cjs exists for the canary tag. but weirdly node still tried to use the require path when doing dynamic import.

lee: Node's conditional exports resolution can be influenced by key order and presence of "main" or "types". If our publish pipeline rewrites package.json keys, that can flip resolver behavior.

jordan: pack-bot, any recent manifest merges?

pack-bot: publish workflow used manifest-merge v2.1. It normalizes JSON keys (alphabetical). Known issue: conditional export object order is not preserved. https://ci.internal/logs/pack/987

sam: oh nice catch. That would explain resolver picking require branch.

lee: short-term: revert canary and republish with a deterministic writer that preserves conditional order. medium-term: add CI unpack + assert exports match expected and add a sample that does dynamic import on node-18.

jordan: also add a note in onboarding doc about verifying sample apps across node LTS versions.

sam: creating the rollback PR and a follow-up that adds the pack-time check. will post when green.
